To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) in conventional rats deprived of their bile secretion, fat absorption decreases by about 50%, 2) this decrease is smaller-that is, about 25%-in germ-free animals, 3) bile deprivation in conventional animals results in a negative digestive balance for stearic acid-that is, the difference between the amounts absorbed and excreted is negative, 4) in germ-free animals, this balance is always positive, 5) biohydrogenation is a very efficient
bile deprivation results in a decrease of dietary fat absorption in conventional rats, but only in a moderate decrease in germ-free rats.
bile deprivation in germ-free as in conventional animals results in an increase in faecal lipids excretion.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the intestinal microflora on fat absorption in the rat, and the influence of bile on the digestive balance of fatty acids.
the study of the role of the gastrointestinal flora in the digestion and the absorption of fat.
the role of bile secretion in the digestive process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

in the rat, bile is essential for the absorption of lipids and the digestion of dietary fatty acids, especially saturated ones, and that the gastrointestinal flora plays a role in the absorption of dietary fatty acids in the rat.

the presence of the gastrointestinal flora, in addition to the absence of bile secretion, is responsible for the decreased absorption of dietary fat in conventional rats deprived of the liver secretion.
bile deprivation in germ-free and in conventional animals resulted in a decrease in the absorption and in an increase in the excretion of dietary lipids.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the gastrointestinal flora is involved in the absorption of dietary fat and that the bile is an important factor in this absorption.

bile deprivation in conventional rats results in a decrease of the absorption of dietary fats, which is mainly due to the decrease of absorption of the most hydrophobic fatty acids, such as palmitic acid (16:0) and stearic acid, and that the difference in the apparent absorption observed in germ-free and convention rats is due to the presence of a more efficient digestive process in the germ-free rat.
the gastrointestinal flora of conventional rats plays a significant role in the absorption and excretion of dietary fat, and that this role is particularly important in bile deprived animals.
The main takeaway from our work is that
bile secretion is required for optimal fat absorption in conventional rats, whereas it is only necessary for the absorption of saturated fatty acids in germfree rats.
the gastrointestinal flora plays an important role in the absorption of dietary fat in conventional animals, especially when bile secretion is impaired.

the presence of gastrointestinal flora in the rat significantly influences the absorption of dietary fats and the excretion pattern of faecal liposoluble compounds when the secretion of bile is prevented.
